title: Production (Railway) ships every main push with no CI gate and no branch protection
current_behavior: Railway's GitHub integration auto-deploys each push to the unprotected main branch; four PRs and everything since reached production without a CI run; all CI workflows and the evaluation gate are advisory because no required status checks exist.
expected_behavior: A merge to main requires green required checks and production deploys only from a CI-verified SHA (control-plane-deploy.yml or Railway 'Wait for CI').
recommendation: Enable branch protection with required checks (Backend test/pip-audit/docker-build, Repo Hygiene, Eval gate, Client/Hostd/Admin on their paths); disable Railway GitHub auto-deploy or enable Wait for CI; set vars.CONTROL_PLANE_DEPLOY_REQUIRED=true so a silent skip fails.

title: GitHub Actions not executing (CB-44): every gate in the repo is inert
current_behavior: Jobs die in 2-4 s with no runner since ~2026-10-28 19:50 UTC; last green Backend CI is dc87beb; every TESTED claim since is local-only; GAP-043 still reads 'proven'.
expected_behavior: Workflows get runners and run to completion on every PR and main push.
recommendation: Owner restores Actions (billing/spending limit); re-run Backend, Client, Hostd, Admin, Repo Hygiene on main; mark GAP-043 regressed.

title: Railway ignores railway.json; deploy settings live only in the dashboard and drift from the repo
current_behavior: railwayConfigFile is null on the production service; the pre-deploy command was fixed by hand in the dashboard; healthcheckPath, restart policy, drainingSeconds and preDeployTimeoutSeconds in railway.json are not applied; tests pin a file production does not read; the F-25 drain budget is unproven on Railway.
expected_behavior: The service links aura_backend/railway.json so deploy behaviour is reviewed in git and pinned by tests, or the file is removed and tests retargeted.
recommendation: Set the service's config file to aura_backend/railway.json, verify the next deploy log shows the /health/live check and the pre-deploy script, and record a dashboard snapshot in docs/reports/.

title: VPS deploy path dead on a stale host-key pin; the VPS's running revision and exposure are unknown
current_behavior: No automated deploy has reached the VPS in ~6 weeks (Host key verification failed since 2026-10-18); the host still holds the production compose, secrets and data; whether the key change was a rebuild or a compromise is unconfirmed; Verify Hosted Inference and VPS Dev Ops share the dead path.
expected_behavior: The VPS is either confirmed out of band, re-pinned and brought to main, or decommissioned with secrets rotated and workflows retired.
recommendation: Confirm the fingerprint out of band, decide the VPS future (CB-03), update deploy/known_hosts by PR and delete deploy/vps_known_hosts.tmp; until then treat the VPS as untrusted and rotate any secret shared with Railway.

title: Whether Celery workers and beat run on Railway is undocumented; background work may be silently absent
evidence: docs/status/BACKEND_STATUS.md (no Railway worker/beat mention; grep lines 115-158 are VPS/F-25 only)
current_behavior: Outbox drain, nightly knowledge refresh, memory consolidation, ingestion and learning queues depend on worker-* and beat services that must be created by hand in the Railway dashboard; nothing in the repo or status docs proves they exist, and no healthcheck or alert covers them on Railway.
expected_behavior: Every production process is enumerated with command, revision and health evidence; a missing worker is visible.
recommendation: List Railway services (railway status) and record them; create the three services per control-plane.md section 2 if absent; surface outbox age in /health/ready or an alert.

title: No metrics scrape, alerting or log retention for the production target; the alert catalogue applies only to the VPS
current_behavior: AuraGatewayDown, AuraAllProvidersUnhealthy, AuraOutboxBacklog, AuraBackupStale, AuraInsecureModeActive and the rest cannot fire for Railway; the F-24 HTTP/outbox metrics have never been scraped on a live target.
expected_behavior: A scrape of the production gateway and a paging route for critical rules.
recommendation: Deploy Prometheus and Alertmanager as Railway services using the existing configs, scrape with AURA_METRICS_TOKEN, route critical alerts to a human, and record one live scrape showing aura_http_* and aura_outbox_*.

title: /metrics is unauthenticated unless AURA_METRICS_TOKEN is set; on Railway the app is the edge and the doc never asks for the token
current_behavior: The metrics route has no auth dependency; protection is opt-in via AURA_METRICS_TOKEN (the code comment records a live probe that found /metrics world-readable on Railway); the Railway variable list omits the token; the VPS relies on nginx deny.
expected_behavior: Metrics reachable only by the scraper on every target.
recommendation: Set AURA_METRICS_TOKEN on the Railway gateway and confirm /metrics returns 401; document the variable in control-plane.md; consider failing validate() rather than warning when the app is the edge.

title: Backup/DR exists only as a VPS compose sidecar; the production datastores on Railway/Qdrant have no repo-owned backup, drill, or RPO/RTO
current_behavior: Production data lives in Railway Postgres (provider snapshots UNKNOWN), a Redis plugin and an external Qdrant; nothing in the repo dumps, encrypts, verifies or restores them; the only drill was a 2026-08-23 sandbox; RPO/RTO never measured.
expected_behavior: Scheduled, encrypted, verified backups of the live Postgres and Qdrant with an off-platform copy and a drill report in docs/reports/.
recommendation: Run the existing backup.sh as a Railway cron/service against the Railway DATABASE_URL and Qdrant URL with an age recipient and S3 target, then execute restore-drill.sh against that output and file the report.

title: Data-encryption and ADR-032 user-key custody on Railway is a single dashboard variable with no documented backup, and the deployment doc omits it
current_behavior: AURA_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEYS, required at boot and (after migration 0019) wrapping every user's data key, exists only as a Railway env var; rotation guidance is VPS-only; losing or regenerating it is total loss of encrypted content; the Railway variable list does not mention it.
expected_behavior: Sealed off-platform key escrow, a Railway rotation runbook, and the variable listed as required in control-plane.md.
recommendation: Export and seal the current keys offline; add AURA_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEYS, AURA_METRICS_TOKEN and AURA_JWT_ISSUER/AUDIENCE to control-plane.md; add a test that the doc lists every production-required variable.

title: Sensitive-class turns have no serving path while hfspace is down on the hosted-primary Railway topology
subsystem: Inference routing on the production target
current_behavior: By ADR-030 policy, documents, memory and tool-output turns may only go to local or hfspace; production has neither healthy (hosted1 only), so those turns are expected to fail while public-content chat succeeds; readiness only reports local_healthy.
expected_behavior: A healthy sensitive-capable provider, or an explicit documented degraded mode visible on /health/ready and alerts.
recommendation: Restore the Space or provision a sensitive-capable provider; have /health/ready report sensitive capability distinctly; alert when no provider admits sensitive content.

title: Deploy Control Plane's readiness and revision probes do not match the app's routes for any plausible RAILWAY_HEALTH_URL
current_behavior: With /health/ready the wait greps for "status" which the payload lacks; with /health/live the version URL becomes .../health/live/health/version (404, 'revision mismatch'); with /health the app 404s. The workflow cannot pass as written once configured.
expected_behavior: Poll /health/live, derive /health/version from the origin, assert git_sha.
recommendation: Compute origin=${RAILWAY_HEALTH_URL%%/health*}, poll $origin/health/live, verify $origin/health/version; add a unit test for the workflow's URL derivation.

title: Deploy-time migration safety relies on an 'additive migrations' assumption the chain no longer satisfies and nothing enforces
current_behavior: Both targets migrate before the new code starts while the old code keeps serving, and rollback reverts the image only; no test or checklist requires expand/contract compatibility or a tested downgrade per revision (only 0017 noted as downgrade-checked).
expected_behavior: Each migration is backward-compatible with the previous image or flagged as needing a maintenance window; downgrade exercised in CI.
recommendation: Add alembic upgrade head && downgrade -1 && upgrade head to the postgres CI job; add a migration-review item to RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md; correct the vps-update.sh comment.

title: Runtime images unpinned or tag-only; the production inference Space builds from vllm/vllm-openai:latest
current_behavior: A Space rebuild picks up whatever vLLM is current; nginx, postgres, redis and tinyproxy float within a tag while observability, ollama, qdrant and the compose vllm service are digest-pinned.
expected_behavior: Every production image pinned by digest with a deliberate bump procedure.
recommendation: Pin vllm/vllm-openai by tag+digest as the compose vllm service does; pin nginx/postgres/redis/tinyproxy by digest; extend test_repo_hygiene.py to assert digests on prod images.

title: Dockerfile CMD lacks --forwarded-allow-ips, so uvicorn ignores Railway's X-Forwarded-Proto/For; the compose command has it
current_behavior: Behind Railway's edge the uvicorn peer is not loopback, so request.url.scheme stays http and request.client is the proxy; rate limiting is unaffected (own X-Forwarded-For parser), but any scheme-derived URL, secure-cookie or HSTS decision would see plain HTTP.
expected_behavior: The platform CMD trusts the single edge hop exactly as the compose command does.
recommendation: Add --forwarded-allow-ips='*' (or FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS) to the Dockerfile CMD and pin it in test_deploy_robustness.py.

title: Tracked deploy/vps_known_hosts.tmp duplicates deploy/known_hosts and is not covered by the artefact guard
current_behavior: A scratch file carrying the stale host-key pin is in the tree and could be mistaken for the authoritative pin.
recommendation: Delete the .tmp file by PR; extend scripts/check_tracked_artifacts.py to refuse *.tmp.
